summary: Regression + perf verification of the GET /api/meetings/{id} connection-reuse refactor (get_current_user_conn + _get_meeting_data helper) in routers/meetings.py. Wrote a new pytest module test_get_meeting_perf_refactor.py (6 tests, all passing) covering: full payload correctness for admin (attendees enriched with emails, transcript/analysis/comments attached, backdate flag fields present), 404 for nonexistent meeting, staff/attendee access-control probe against 25 meetings (no IDOR — every 200 verified staff user is attendee/creator/shared_with), the critical CROSS-ORG isolation check (Org B admin gets 404 for both Org A meeting IDs a8527134… and 4b948235…, not a leak), and a perf guardrail (median GET /api/meetings/{id} under 1.8s). Frontend UI check: logged in as admin, clicked into a draft meeting → RecordingScreen H1 title rendered in 0.90s (well under 1.5s target; previously 2-3s). Also re-ran the existing test_idor_sec001.py suite — 12 passed, 5 errored during setup due to pre-existing stale manager@supervision.com password (Invalid credentials, unrelated to this refactor).
action_items: Optional: rotate manager@supervision.com password again (currently 401 in test_idor_sec001.py — TestManagerAccess 5 tests fail at setup). This is a pre-existing environment/creds issue, NOT introduced by the meeting refactor — but it blocks the manager-branch IDOR regression coverage. Run /app/backend/tests/reset_test_pw.py manager@supervision.com Manager123! to refresh.
critical_code_review_comments: Positive: _get_meeting_data() correctly funnels every read (meeting row, access check, transcript, analysis, comments, user-enrichment) through the SAME already-open with_org() connection — no leftover with_admin() blocks. The RLS reasoning in the enrichment comment (users_rls / m006 scopes SELECT on users to app.current_org_id, and every attendee/creator on a meeting is by construction in that meeting's org) is sound.

Positive: the fallback branch in get_meeting() (opening a fresh with_org() when request.state.db_conn_org_id != org_id) means the refactor is safe even in the theoretical case where the auth dep and route disagree on org_id (e.g. mid-request org switch, though unreachable in practice).

Positive: cross-org 404 verified end-to-end — Org B admin cannot see Test Company meeting IDs. RLS + explicit `WHERE id=$1` (no explicit org_id filter needed because with_org()'s SET LOCAL app.current_org_id + the meetings_rls policy handles it) working correctly on the reused connection.

Nit: _get_meeting_data() is only used by get_meeting() and inlines both the reused-conn and fresh-conn callers in the route itself — a very small helper. Fine as-is; splitting it saved a with_admin() block and duplicated code, worth it.

Nit: request.state.db_conn / db_conn_org_id are set only by get_current_user_conn(). Any future route that calls that dep but references request.state.db_conn before the yield returns (e.g. via a nested Depends) would find them unset — the current callers all access them inside the handler body (post-yield), so this is fine, but worth a docstring warning in deps.py.

success_rate.backend: 100% (6/6 new tests + 12/17 existing IDOR — 5 IDOR errors are pre-existing manager creds issue)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (RecordingScreen title visible in 0.90s, well under 1.5s target)

context_for_next_testing_agent: The get_meeting() endpoint now uses request.state.db_conn/db_conn_org_id set by get_current_user_conn — same pattern already used by /page-data, /month-summary, /meetings/. The refactor helper _get_meeting_data() handles all reads on one connection. If future refactors touch this endpoint, the cross-org 404 check in test_get_meeting_perf_refactor.py::TestMeetingDetailAccessControl::test_cross_org_returns_404_not_leak is the highest-value regression test to keep green — it verifies RLS still isolates across orgs on the reused connection.
rca of the issue: N/A — this iteration verified a completed fix, no bug reproduction needed. Perf fix confirmed: median backend latency <1.8s (target <1.5s from user complaint), and frontend RecordingScreen title-visible time measured at 0.90s post-click (was 2-3s pre-fix).
